CVE-2026-123339.description:
Improper trust of forwarded headers in RouterListener::onKernelFinishRequest() in Symfony HttpKernel versions prior to 5.4.56, 6.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11 allows a remote attacker to control the host, scheme, and port of absolute URLs generated for the rest of the request, poisoning links in pages stored by a shared cache and in e-mails sent after the page was rendered.When a page renders an inline fragment (render() in Twig, or an ESI tag rendered inline), SubRequestHandler temporarily adds 127.0.0.1 to the trusted proxies, and RouterListener rebuilds the router context from the main request while that trust is still active, so the X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded headers of a request whose client address is 127.0.0.1 are trusted even though that address is not a configured trusted proxy. From that point on, every absolute URL the router generates for the rest of the main request takes its host, scheme, and port from headers sent by the client, including URLs produced by url() in Twig and by UrlGeneratorInterface::ABSOLUTE_URL.

Applications are affected when they are reached over HTTP from 127.0.0.1, for example behind a TLS terminator, reverse proxy, local HTTP cache, or sidecar proxy on the same host, and that proxy passes the client’s forwarded headers along. With the default configuration (framework.trusted_proxies unset), all forwarded headers, including X-Forwarded-Host, are trusted during that window. Applications served through php-fpm, mod_php, or a proxy on another host are not affected. When framework.trusted_hosts is configured, a forwarded host outside the list is rejected, but the scheme and port can still be changed.

CVE-2026-135804.description:
The fix for CVE-2026-45756 lowers pcre.backtrack_limit to 10000 around each preg_match() call of the match() and search() filter functions. That limit applies to one starting position, not to one call. PCRE resets its counter at every position it tries a match from. So an unanchored pattern that stays just under the limit is paid once per byte of the subject. Each call also starts from a fresh limit, so chaining clauses in one filter multiplies the work.

Two other paths made the cost of a query grow faster than its size, without any regular expression:
- The filter evaluator scanned the whole expression for logical operators once per node. Its cost grew with the square of the number of chained clauses.
- Queries starting with $ inside a filter, like @.x == $.limit or length($.items), were evaluated again for every node the filter visits.

An application that evaluates an attacker-influenced JSONPath expression can therefore still be made to hold a PHP worker. A document of 2 MB and a query of 2.5 KB take 3.5 minutes of CPU.

JsonCrawler::find() now bounds the total regex work of one call, and throws an exception when that budget is exhausted. Filter expressions are parsed once per query, and absolute queries inside filters are evaluated once per query.

CVE-2026-121373.description:
The Symfony HtmlSanitizer component MetaRefreshAttributeSanitizer, introduced to fix CVE-2026-48761, sanitizes the refresh URL of content attributes of meta tags using a regular expression that is too narrow, allowing sanitization to be bypassed, and resulting in potential URL redirection to untrusted sites in Symfony versions 6.1.x prior to 6.4.50, 7.x prior to 7.4.23, and 8.x prior to 8.1.11.




The shared declarative refresh steps in the WHATWG HTML Standard require a broader approach: the separator after the time may be ASCII whitespace alone, with no ; or ,, and the url= keyword is optional. Directives the browser honours, but the regular expression misses are returned unchanged, so the attacker URL skips UrlSanitizer entirely and both allowLinkSchemes and allowLinkHosts are defeated for the refresh navigation.




This is reachable under any configuration that allows meta with http-equiv and content, including the documented allowStaticElements() preset.

In Symfony Expression Language versions prior to 5.4.54, 6.4.48, 7.4.21, and 8.1.9, the parser of the ExpressionLanguage component built its node tree with no bound on its depth. Broadcom has released security updates for vCenter and ESX. The affected vCenter branches are fixed in 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0300 and 9.1.2. There is currently no confirmed exploitation of these newly disclosed vulnerabilities, but administrators should prioritise patching and review their exposure.

posts.content: CVE-2026-90069 Linux kernel crypto acomp bug: cloning async requests underallocates context, letting QAT write past the stack buffer. CVSS 7.8. Patch available, update now. #CVE #infosec #Linux https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-90069/

CVE-2026-90069.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

crypto: acomp - allocate async request context when cloning

ACOMP_REQUEST_ON_STACK() reserves only enough storage for the
synchronous fallback. When an async implementation is selected, callers
clone that stack request before retrying, but acomp_request_clone()
currently copies only the stack-sized object. The clone therefore has no
storage for the async provider request context, and providers such as QAT
write past the allocation through acomp_request_ctx(). KASAN does report
a slab OOB write.

Allocate a zeroed clone large enough for the runtime acomp request size,
copy only the bytes present in the source object, and preserve the
existing fallback-on-allocation-failure behavior. Use the runtime reqsize
because an implementation may adjust it during tfm initialization.

🚨 BREAKING: VMWARE HAS DISCLOSED ANOTHER CRITICAL VCENTER AUTHENTICATION BYPASS, JUST FIVE DAYS AFTER PATCHING A ZERO-DAY EXPLOITED BY CHINA-LINKED HACKERS.

Tracked as CVE-2026-123903 (CVSS 9.8), the new vulnerability allows attackers with network access to bypass authentication in VMware Directory Service (vmdir) without knowing a password. A public proof of concept is already available, and Broadcom says there is NO workaround.

And that's not the only problem. Broadcom's latest security advisory, VMSA-2026-0011, addresses 23 vulnerabilities, including two additional critical flaws, CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911, that could allow attackers to execute malicious code directly on ESX hosts. No VM credentials or initial access inside a virtual machine are required.

This is the THIRD distinct vCenter authentication bypass disclosed in roughly four months.

Broadcom has released security updates for vCenter and ESX. The affected vCenter branches are fixed in 8.0 U3m, 9.0.2.0300 and 9.1.2. There is currently no confirmed exploitation of these newly disclosed vulnerabilities, but administrators should prioritise patching and review their exposure.

Full technical breakdown, public PoC details, affected versions and patches ↓

CVE-2026-54577.description: mport is the MidnightBSD Package Manager. Prior to 2.7.8, the audit command in mport/mport.c computed option-adjusted local_argv and local_argc values but passed the original argument entry to audit_package(). When an operator or automation used an option such as -r before a package name, stale optind state and the unadjusted argument could cause mport to audit the option token instead of the requested package, producing a false-negative or useless result that could leave a vulnerable package unidentified. The corrected parsing resets optind and optreset before using the adjusted local arguments. This issue is fixed in version 2.7.8.

CVE-2026-96889.description:
Librsvg uses libxml2, a C library, to parse XML.  When librsvg parses
an SVG document which has a nested Xinclude, an XML entity declaration
with a duplicate name as an existing one can cause a use-after-free error.

While libxml2 is expanding an internal entity, a recursive XInclude
can parse another document that declares an entity with the same
name. Both parses use the same `XmlState` entity
map on the librsvg side. `entity_insert()` replaces the first entry, whose `Drop`
implementation calls `xmlFreeNode()`. The outer `xmlCtxtParseEntity()`
then keeps using the freed 144-byte `xmlEntity`.

The included parse should not free an entity that the outer parser is still using.

The fix is in commit 8a1b0cd319e9af2d1e9cf878081dd77f227a0504, where
librsvg will no longer free xmlEntity pointers that libxml2 is still
using.

Prior to 1.11.3, sofia_presence_handle_sip_i_message() split the To user of an inbound SIP MESSAGE on a plus sign and treated the left side as a chat protocol selector. Selecting the api chat proto reached switch_api_execute(), allowing a peer whose MESSAGE was accepted to run FreeSWITCH API commands, including operating-system command sinks, with the daemon's privileges. CVE-2026-90052.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

dm-integrity: fix buffer overflow with keyed discard

Since commit 68c5c42567bc ("dm-integrity: replace forgeable discard
filler with a keyed sector marker"), integrity_metadata computes a
checksum for every discarded block into the "checksums" buffer.
integrity_sector_checksum always writes the whole digest. So if the tag
size is smaller than the digest size, the checksum of the last block
that fits into the buffer is written past the end of it. For example,
with hmac(sha256) and tag size 16, a 4MiB discard writes 16 bytes past
the kmalloc'ed page.

Fix this by subtracting extra_space from the buffer size when computing
max_blocks, like we do for writes.

CVE-2026-44908.description: Improper following of a certificate’s chain of trust in the remote-attestation verifier used to establish trust with Meta AI's confidential computing backend in WhatsApp for iOS before 2.26.24.72, WhatsApp Business for iOS and WhatsApp for Mac Desktop before v2.26.23.72, WhatsApp for Android before v2.26.23.74, and WhatsApp Business for Android before v2.26.23.70 could have allowed someone positioned within Meta infrastructure to bypass the hardware root of trust by presenting clients with a VCEK certificate signed by a key other than the hardware manufacturer’s. Any such VCEK Cert would first have to be published to the third-party binary transparency ledger used by WhatsApp Private Processing. The ledger shows that every published VCEK certificate chains to the hardware root of trust, confirming no exploitation.
